audit.whatIsWrong: The combo that actually kills Rumble in this lane is never stated: Fling roots the target if it lands them in Mega Adhesive. The text treats Fling and Mega Adhesive as two separate nuisances. It also claims 'one clean Fling erases your Scrap Shield', which nothing in Fling does, and the content 'early' paragraph calls Fling his W.
audit.why: Riot's Fling description: 'Damages target enemy unit and flings them into the air behind Singed. If the target Singed flings lands in his Mega Adhesive, they are also rooted.' That makes Mega Adhesive (W, 17s at rank 1, 1000 range) the ability to track — not Fling, which is 10s at rank 1 and only 125 range. The whole defensive rule collapses into one line: do not stand on the goo, and Fling is a shove instead of a death sentence. Rumble has no dash and no cleanse, so a root inside a full Poison Trail is the losing sequence.

Also: _missing-interactions.json emits a 'both sides carry displacement (Scrap Shield (W) vs Fling (E))' rule for this pair. Only Singed displaces — Rumble's Scrap Shield is a shield plus a movement-speed burst, and its knockup and terrain flags in the kit file are parsing misfires. I did not write the mutual-displacement line. Separately, Mega Adhesive grounds, and grounding is normally understood to block Flash as well as dashes — I left that out of the copy because Riot's text says only 'slowing and grounding' and the kit's needsResearch fields are empty, so I could not verify the Flash interaction from the data available.
